title: Deprecation cadence & migration ops playbook: guided cutovers, release notes, and concierge support
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: Define an operational playbook to retire legacy model tags and runtime endpoints with minimal customer disruption. This ticket coordinates cross-functional launch planning for a three-stage deprecation: announcement, migration runway, and enforced cutover. Deliverables: coordinated release notes, in-console notices and SDK warnings, a migration guide + automation scripts, a concierge outreach program for high-value customers, dashboards to monitor migration progress, and a post-cutover rollback/incident plan.
rollout_timeline: Phase 0 - Internal readiness (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-15): finalize PRD, confirm ENG readiness, draft release notes and migration guide
Phase 1 - Public announcement & docs publish (2026-03-16): blog + in-product banner + email to affected customers; publish migration guide and SDK warnings
Phase 2 - Migration runway (2026-03-16 to 2026-04-14): automatic compatibility shims active; weekly migration reports; concierge outreach begins for customers > $5k/mo
Phase 3 - Canary cutover (2026-04-15 to 2026-04-20): route 5% traffic to new model variants for low-risk customers and monitor SLOs
Phase 4 - Enforced cutover (2026-04-21): legacy endpoints retired; customers routed to pinned variants or blocked with upgrade instructions; support escalation window 72 hours
Phase 5 - Post-cutover observability & refunds (2026-04-22 to 2026-05-06): measure regressions, open incident retro, optional customer remediation steps
communication_assets: Release notes checklist: purpose, timeline, impact table, required actions by customer, links to migration guide, rollback plan
Email template - initial notice: subject and body for affected customers (concise impact + next steps + contact path)
In-console banner copy and dismiss rules + product route to 'Learn how to migrate'
SDK deprecation warning format and upgrade instructions (npm/pip/snippets)
Support playbook: triage steps, escalation matrix, canned responses, SLO rollback triggers
Community post and changelog entry templates for public channels
migration_guides: Quickstart: 5-minute migration for standard usage patterns (code samples for text generation, chat and embeddings)
Edge cases: managing KV cache behavior and batching across pinned model variants
Compatibility shim details: what is auto-mapped, what requires manual prompt changes
SDK changelog: breaking changes and suggested migration snippets
Checklist for enterprises: ACLs, VPC routing, key rotation guidance
Automation: one-click customer migration script (GitHub link) and Rollback DSL for eng ops
rollout_gates: Gate A - Eng signoff: unit/regression tests green, canary automation in place
Gate B - Observability: dashboards for latency, error-rate, quality-regressions published
Gate C - Docs & support readiness: migration guide published, support playbook validated
Gate D - Compliance: enterprise customers with contracts flagged and legal notified where required
acceptance_criteria: All public-facing release notes and migration docs published and linked in console
SDK warnings deployed to major package registries and documented in changelog
Automated migration scripts available in customer repo and tested on staging
Concierge outreach initiated for all customers in high-impact cohort
Migration completion metric baseline established and dashboards live
No Sev1 incidents during canary cutover for 72 hours before enforced cutover
metrics_and_alerts: Migration completion rate by customer cohort (target > 80% by due_date)
Error rate delta on new model variants (alert if > +0.5% absolute)
Support ticket volume for deprecation category (alert if > 3x baseline)
Quality regression monitor: evals on canonical prompt set (alert if median drop > 2%)

risks: High-value customers dependent on legacy endpoints may have bespoke integrations
Automated compatibility shim may not cover custom prompt engineering patterns
Uncaught quality regressions for long-context workloads after cutover
Insufficient observability for low-volume enterprise tenants
Timing conflicts with other major releases may amplify support load
mitigations: Run targeted migration tests with top 20 customers before public announcement
Provide a holdback option and extended runway for enterprise customers (by contract)
Maintain canary rollback playbook and immediate fallback route to legacy service for first 72 hours
Create a temporary dedicated 'deprecation' Slack channel staffed by cross-functional on-call
Stage throttled cutover windows per region to distribute load
